title: Efficacy and safety of intravitreal injection of aflibercept biosimilar for treating diabetic macular edema

license.statement: CC BY (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)'; no version or URL given in the licence element)

groups.agent: aflibercept biosimilar QL1207 2 mg/0.05 mL intravitreal
groups.description: Newly diagnosed, previously untreated DME (Zibo Central Hospital, February to April 2024, retrospective), 40 eyes of 33 patients: three injections at 4-week intervals, then PRN (3+PRN). Inclusion required complete clinical data and all patients completed a minimum follow-up of 6 months.

decision: excluded: no admissible series (the only tabulated acuity series is a complete-case set: complete clinical data and a minimum 6-month follow-up equal to the last tabulated visit)

exclusions.what: Table 1 (tab1) BCVA (LogMAR) at baseline ('Preoperation') and 1, 3 and 6 months, 40 eyes
exclusions.reason: complete-case analysis set: inclusion criterion (c) required the availability of complete clinical data and the Abstract and Methods state that the patients completed a minimum follow-up of 6 months, which is the last tabulated visit; the article does not state that no treated eye was left out (protocol inclusion 5; brief complete-case ruling)

exclusions.what: Table 1 p-value rows and Table 2 (tab2) p-values between follow-up visits
Table 3 (tab3) FAZ area, vascular density and mfERG amplitude

exclusions.reason: text values of the same excluded analysis set

notes: Table 1 states BCVA in logMAR as mean +/- SD with no Snellen or decimal row (reinjection criteria mention Snellen lines; the Statistical Analysis says BCVA was converted to logMAR); the unit and statistic would be admissible, but the analysis set is complete-case.
Central retinal thickness (Table 1), FAZ, vascular density and mfERG (Table 3) and injection counts are reported in the article and mentioned here only.
No record is written: the study has no admissible series under extraction protocol 1.0.0 and the extraction brief.
